observations: The brand 'really H-POWER' and model 'GF4600' are printed on the front control panel.
The control panel features an engine switch, a voltmeter, two AC outlets, a circuit breaker, and DC terminals.
The unit is sitting on a white plastic sheet, suggesting it is recently unpacked.
The frame is black tubular steel.
The fuel tank is yellow with a black cap and a fuel gauge.

claims.evidence: The item looks clean and is on plastic, but internal engine wear or previous use cannot be confirmed remotely.
The technical specification plate showing the KVA rating is not visible.
The side of the generator where the recoil starter (pull cord) would be is not shown.
The material of the alternator windings cannot be determined from photos.

risks.risk: Generator may not start or produce electricity
risks.proof: A video of the generator starting and powering a high-draw appliance like an electric iron.

risks.risk: Alternator may have aluminum windings instead of copper
risks.proof: A clear photo of the technical specification plate or a close-up of the windings through the alternator vents.

risks.risk: Actual power output may be lower than 4.5kva
risks.proof: A photo of the silver technical specification plate usually found on the side of the alternator.

proof_requests: Photo of the technical specification plate on the side of the generator.
Video of the generator running and powering a load.
Photo of the side showing the pull-start mechanism.
response.reason: The brand and model are clearly identified from the photos, allowing for a valuation based on the worst-case scenario of it being a non-functional unit with aluminum windings.
